titulo: 7 formas de usar o Claude Code para tocar um negócio sem saber programar

titulo: Z2RAM Claims SRAM Memory Speeds at Much Greater Density
resumo: Pat Gelsinger is familiar with the graveyard of failed memory technologies. “We haven’t had a new memory for three decades,” says the former Intel CEO. SRAM, DRAM, and flash memory still dominate. Gelsinger has witnessed the rise and fall of several potential alternatives—most recently Optane , Intel’s failed attempt to create “universal memory.” But Gelsinger, who is now a general partner at venture capital firm Playground , believes that AI is forcing a rethink of the entire computing stack—and that memory is a key part of that shift. Playground has backed Nagare Labs , a company spun out of Georgia Tech working on a prototype memory technology called Z2RAM. Instead of replacing existing memory, Z2RAM will attempt to offer a new layer in the existing memory stack that could prove useful for AI workloads and for other tasks that benefit from low latencies. “This is an SRAM addition, rather than a DRAM replacement,” says Suman Datta , a Georgia Tech professor and former Intel transistor researcher.
